# `Q-2-42` — Invalid conditional content attribute

> A `.content-visible` / `.content-hidden` element carries a condition
> Quarto does not recognize, or carries both marker classes at once.

## What this means

Conditional content lets one source file produce different output for
different formats or profiles:

```markdown
::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
Only readers of the HTML version see this.
:::
```

Quarto recognizes exactly six conditions:

| Condition        | True when                                              |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `when-format`    | the output format matches                              |
| `unless-format`  | the output format does not match                       |
| `when-profile`   | the named project profile is active                    |
| `unless-profile` | the named project profile is not active                |
| `when-meta`      | the dotted metadata path is present and not `false`    |
| `unless-meta`    | the dotted metadata path is absent or `false`          |

This warning fires in two situations. Either the element carries an
attribute that starts with `when-` or `unless-` but is not one of those
six — in which case the attribute is ignored — or the element carries
both `.content-visible` and `.content-hidden`, which is contradictory.

Both cases are quiet failures, which is why Quarto reports them.
Quarto 1 ignores an unrecognized condition silently, so a typo turns
into content that is unconditionally visible with no indication that
the condition you wrote was never consulted.

## Why this happens

- **A typo in the condition name.** `when-formats`, `when-format-is`,
  and `unless-formats` all look right and all do nothing.
- **A condition borrowed from a different feature.** `when-meta` reads
  document metadata; there is no `when-var`, `when-env`, or
  `when-lang`.
- **Both marker classes on one element**, usually from editing a
  `.content-hidden` block into a `.content-visible` one and leaving
  the old class behind. The element is treated as `.content-hidden`.

## How to fix

Correct the condition to one of the six recognized spellings:

```markdown
::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
PDF-only content.
:::
```

If you meant to key off document metadata, use `when-meta` with a
dotted path into the merged metadata:

```markdown
::: {.content-visible when-meta="draft"}
Visible while `draft: true` is set in the front matter.
:::
```

If the element carries both marker classes, delete the one you did not
intend:

```markdown
<!-- before: contradictory -->
::: {.content-visible .content-hidden when-format="html"}

<!-- after -->
::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
```

## Example

```markdown
::: {.content-visible when-formats="html"}
This paragraph is *always* visible: `when-formats` is not a condition,
so nothing constrains the block.
:::
```

Removing the trailing `s` makes the condition take effect.
